scope: Original archive bytes and manuscript contents are not redistributed in this deliverable. Review summaries and newly generated certificates are included.

archives.novelty_comparison: Claims 26 quintic CM coefficient fields and a prime-degree bijection using unconditional CM/class-number inputs; also genus containment, weighted races and S3 reductions. These are prior results, not new results of the present analysis. Its S3 arithmetic estimate remains unproved.

Claims the 229-field classification of an abelian sufficient zero-sum condition and arithmetic representation bounds; proves completely-split and Kummer one-sided reformulations and an exact upper endpoint without linear independence. The numerical classification was not independently rerun here, and the nonabelian inequalities remain unproved.

Contains scalar determinant amplification, a Landau criterion, and a conductor-23 cubic reduction; seven elementary algebraic Lean lemmas have recorded checking logs. The analytic cubic prime estimate is a missing hypothesis. Present work does not reannounce these scalar criteria as new.

Contains the sparse auxiliary-family criterion, a higher-pole scalar criterion, a pure-Tate inertia obstruction, and products-before-gcds quantifier control. It does not construct the missing nonabelian arithmetic family or prove Vandiver/K-group vanishing.

Proves exponent-six completeness on omega(|D|)<=6 or |D|/Pmax<=1e8, mod-4 all-scale ramp bias, and a conductor-23 sign equivalence. It explicitly proposes smaller genus fields plus small ramified ideals; the current intermediate-genus certificate answers that limited follow-up and strengthens the exclusion families without a full classification.

claim_boundaries: The new genus theorem is a human mathematical proof and an extension relative to the five reviewed packets; publication priority is not asserted.
The certificate script verifies finite rational inequalities and the example, not GRH, class field theory, the prime-bound proof, or the global EKN census.
The genus intermediate field is multiquadratic over Q, so only Dirichlet GRH is invoked.
The original source construction and these new extensions have not received a new full Lean build in this workspace.
The current work does not claim complete exponent-six classification or a newly resolved named nonabelian RH conjecture.
